sections.heading: C — Driving record and enforcement
sections.markdown:
## C — Driving record and enforcement

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
PennDOT keeps a driving record for each licensed Pennsylvania driver, including offense and conviction reports from police and courts. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
Certain guilty findings add points, and PennDOT begins corrective action at six or more points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
The first accumulation of at least six points brings written notice requiring a special written point examination. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
After dropping below six and reaching at least six again, the driver must attend a Departmental hearing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
Further accumulations of six or more points can bring additional hearings or suspensions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
A driver younger than eighteen is suspended for reaching six points or being convicted of exceeding the limit by at least 26 mph. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
For those under-eighteen triggers, the first suspension is ninety days and later occurrences are 120 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
Three points are removed after each twelve consecutive months without a point-assigning violation or suspension or revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
After a record remains at zero for twelve consecutive months, a new accumulation is treated as the first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A01
DUI, vehicle-related felony or homicide, reckless driving and highway racing are among convictions causing suspension or revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A01
Fleeing police, driving while suspended or revoked, lights-off identification evasion and hit-and-run are listed sanctionable convictions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A01
A second or later unlicensed-driving offense within five years is listed as a suspension or revocation trigger. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A01
Failure to stop for a school bus with red flashers and an extended arm brings a sixty-day suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A01
Disregarding a rail-crossing gate or barrier brings a thirty-day suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A01
A sanction notice is mailed with its starting date, and the listed license, permit or camera card must be returned by that date. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A02
A sanction begins on the notice's effective date, regardless of when the license or acknowledgment is surrendered. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A02
Early surrender does not begin the sanction early. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A02
A sanction appeal goes to the county Court of Common Pleas Civil Division within thirty days of the notice's mailing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A02
Restoration requires completing the sanction and all applicable restoration requirements. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A02
A restored record normally carries five points, except a fifteen-day second-six-point suspension or suspension for not responding to a citation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A02
Keep liability insurance continuously on a registered vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A02
An insurance lapse of at least 31 days brings a three-month registration suspension; operating or permitting use uninsured also brings three months of driving suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A02
Restoring uninsured-vehicle privileges requires proof of current coverage and the restoration fees. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A02
At a police traffic stop, follow the officer's directions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A02
Signal and stop as close to the right edge as safely possible, parking away from traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A02
After stopping, turn off the engine and radio and lower the window to communicate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A02
At night, turn the interior light on before the officer approaches. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A02
Keep movements limited, do not reach for items and keep driver and passenger hands visible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A02
Immediately tell the officer if any firearm is being transported. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A02
Remain inside with doors closed unless asked to exit, and keep the belt fastened until the officer observes it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A02
Wait for a request before retrieving license, registration or insurance documents; hand over the requested items rather than the wallet. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A02
Remain polite and contest a disputed citation through a court hearing rather than arguing at the scene. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A02
A concern about officer conduct can be raised later with a police-department supervisor. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F34 | anchor: A03
If uncertain about a stopping vehicle's police identity, acknowledge with hazards and reduced speed while proceeding to the nearest well-lit populated place. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F35 | anchor: A03
Ask for identification if the stopping person is not uniformed or uses an unmarked vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F36 | anchor: A03
Police vehicles may display red and blue or red alone when unmarked, with white lights in addition; blue alone does not identify a police officer. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

Misconceptions: refusing testing can have consequences separate from a DUI conviction; a BAC below the adult threshold does not rule out DUI; submitting a license early does not start a sanction early.
Mnemonics: know the record, respond to notices, stop safely and report crashes.
Glossary: revocation removes a driving privilege; ARD is Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition; DLC coordinates member-jurisdiction driver records.
Dynamic facts: no officeholder, local answer or time-varying value is asserted; handbook edition currency is tracked as source debt in the authority part.
